prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: hit while turning left in Pasadena, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported shoulder injury. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1175; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text: Driver 1 was traveling in the left-hand lane and began a left turn at the intersection when the front of the vehicle was struck by Driver 2, who was proceeding straight through the same intersection. On arrival, I observed heavy front-end damage to Driver 1's vehicle, including a crushed bumper, a displaced hood, and a deployed airbag, all consistent with the direction and force of the impact described by both drivers. Passenger was seated in the front passenger position and was able to describe the sequence of events. Driver 1 reported pain in the right shoulder and was evaluated at the scene by emergency medical personnel, and the nature of the injury fits the forces typical of this type of collision. Photographs taken at the scene confirm the position of the vehicles and the damage described, but no independent witnesses were located. Records available to me show no prior damage to Driver 1's vehicle. Driver 1 is listed as a member of the household of the registered policyholder and was operating the vehicle with permission.
